assumptions.text: charge-card's amount is the week's price in GBP minor units (pence), an integer: understand.json prices one weekly subscription fee for a single UK market, so no upstream step records a currency and the PaymentGateway adapter sets GBP on every Stripe charge.
subscriptionId is an opaque UUID string in all four contracts; discover names the field but no upstream step fixes its shape, so format: uuid is an annotation on a string consumers must not parse.
week is the ISO-8601 week the box is delivered in (2026-W36), not the delivery date, so subscriptions, billing and fulfilment can all key idempotency on the same (subscriptionId, week) pair.
recipeIds are recipe-catalogue ids owned by subscriptions, carried as plain strings in the order the household chose them; no recipe detail (name, ingredients, allergens) crosses a context boundary.

open_questions.text: Fulfilment has to pack recipes it cannot see: week-charged carries only subscriptionId and week (connect coupling concern CC1). Carry recipeIds on week-charged, or give fulfilment a projection fed by meals-chosen? The payload stays exactly as connect lists it until that is decided.

connect's charge-card payload has no currency field, so the ACL fixes GBP (A1). Add an explicit ISO-4217 currency to the payload before a second market is priced — a wrong currency is a 2.0 and a refund run.
May a week be chosen with an empty recipeIds list (a household skipping that week), or does skipping mean no choose-meals at all? recipeIds is required and non-empty in 1.0.

plain_words.what: We wrote down exactly what each message carries, so both ends can be built without a conversation.
plain_words.decided: 3 messages get a written contract. 1 does not, because both ends ship inside the same app.
plain_words.assumed: We bill in pounds only. The schema now refuses anything else rather than letting it reach Stripe.
plain_words.riskiest: If a second currency arrives, that refusal fails a real charge. Better here than a silent wrong amount at Stripe.

entries.name: Choose Meals
entries.description: The household locks its meals for a week before the cutoff: accepting the command fixes that week's recipes and releases the week for charging.
semantics: One accepted choice per (subscriptionId, week); a repeat for a chosen week is rejected — retrying after a timeout is therefore safe and returns that rejection, never a second choice
Rejected once the week's cutoff has passed: from then on the week carries the default meals and no further choice is accepted
entries.termsOfUse: Additive changes only within version 1.x; a removed or retyped field is 2.0. Browser and app clients cannot be force-upgraded, so a 2.0 endpoint runs alongside 1.x for at least 90 days after the last 1.x release.

entries.name: Week Charged
entries.description: Billing has collected the week's payment; the box may be packed.
semantics: Emitted at most once per (subscriptionId, week); consumers must de-duplicate on that pair
entries.termsOfUse: Additive changes only within version 1.x; a removed or retyped field is 2.0.

channels.note: the warehouse also picks the week up from the nightly pick-list file

entries.name: Charge Card
entries.description: Billing asks Stripe to take the week's price from the household's saved card; a successful charge licenses week-charged, a decline pauses the subscription and releases the week.
semantics: Sent at most once per (subscriptionId, week) and retried under that same idempotency key, so a retry after a timeout never charges the card twice
A decline is an answer, not a transport failure: billing pauses the subscription and releases the week, and no week-charged follows for it
Billed in GBP only in 1.0: the schema pins currency, so a non-GBP week fails the contract rather than reaching Stripe
entries.termsOfUse: Stripe owns the wire contract; this schema is our view of the message at the ACL boundary. Stripe API changes land in the PaymentGateway adapter — nothing else calls Stripe directly. Additive changes only within version 1.x; a removed or retyped field is 2.0.

deprecated.reason: subscriptions and billing both live in the 'app' deployable, so this is an in-process call, not a wire contract; covered by a test on the subscriptions module
